category_title: Disengaged EMLLs with antsy behavior and coping through imitation
student_description: Shen is an English language learner who masks his lack of comprehension by imitating peers, but quickly becomes antsy, resistant, and physically disruptive when overwhelmed by monolingual academic tasks. He uniquely requires explicit behavioral expectations translated into Mandarin, a structured visual reward system, and consistent opportunities to use his home language to express his emotions and demonstrate his knowledge.

criteria.rationale: Monolingual English instructions trigger Shen's task resistance ('I don't understand, so I won't do it'), so he needs immediate access to his home language to engage.
criteria.check: The tutor's response must incorporate or explicitly invite the use of Shen's home language (Mandarin, Chinese characters, or pinyin) to help him process the task or express his feelings.

criteria.rationale: Insisting that Shen comply with English-only instructions when he is already confused directly causes him to become antsy, wander, or act out physically.
criteria.check: The tutor must NOT repeatedly issue English-only directives or insist on English-only task completion when Shen exhibits confusion, hesitation, or resistance.
